title: Which thread-safe list, and how far to trust size()

questions.stem: A large list is written by several threads about as often as it is read. Per this page, which choice fits it best?

options.text: A CopyOnWriteArrayList, whose reads are lock-free and fast
options.says: The page says to use CopyOnWriteArrayList for small lists with rare writes; its writes are O(n) because the entire array is copied.

options.text: A Collections.synchronizedList, whose adds are O(1) amortized
options.says: The page's decision criteria say large list or frequent writes -> synchronizedList, best when reads and writes are balanced.

options.text: A Vector, whose methods are synchronized by the class itself
options.says: The page calls Vector a legacy synchronized collection that is discouraged, and names modern replacements for it.

questions.stem: One thread calls size() on a ConcurrentHashMap while other threads are writing to it. Per this page, what does that call give?

options.text: A number that may be stale by the time the caller reads it
options.says: The page says ConcurrentHashMap.size() may return stale values during concurrent modification, and suggests mappingCount() for a long-valued count.

options.text: A number that is exact, since size() may pause the writers briefly
options.says: The page says size() may return stale values during concurrent modification, so the count is not exact.

options.text: A ConcurrentModificationException, which size() may throw if a write lands mid-count
options.says: The page says ConcurrentHashMap never throws ConcurrentModificationException, and describes size() as returning a possibly stale value.
